page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6448H processor operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features a shared CPU allocation with 32 vCPUs and no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 375.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.72 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 2200 GB NVMe SSD.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 62,892.75 and a Passmark CPU score of 64,768.69. The system demonstrates top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing 13,643.47 tokens per second for prompts and 348.06 tokens per second for generation on a small 135M model, alongside 6,275.36 tokens per second for prompts on a medium 7B model. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 4,985.78 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 211.9 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, though large-block write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by bundling massive GPU memory, substantial system RAM, and fast NVMe storage into a single node, reducing the need for multi-node clustering for moderately sized models. The hardware profile is optimized for GPU-accelerated workloads, including LLM inference, machine learning model training, and data science jobs. The strong database performance, highlighted by 70.17 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, also makes it suitable for high-throughput database operations and real-time analytics.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a high-density Cloud GPU server powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs. It features 375.0 GB of system memory and a 2200 GB NVMe SSD. The server's primary compute acceleration comes from two NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference, with prompt processing speeds of 6,275.36 tokens per second on a 7B model, and strong multi-core CPU capabilities. While large-block memory write bandwidth is average, the system excels in memory read bandwidth and database operations, registering 70.17 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. This hardware configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, data science, and memory-intensive database workloads.
